title: Cryo tank pressure / temperature divergence
body: Any sudden cryo tank pressure or temperature divergence > 3 sigma from steady-state shall be reported to the Flight Director and the affected tank isolated pending diagnosis. Co-locate fuel-cell reactant supply check on remaining tank.
citation: Apollo Operations Handbook, Block II CSM, §5.9 + Mission Rules MSC-PA-FR-69

title: Loss of two of three fuel cells
body: If two of three CSM fuel cells lose reactant supply or drop bus voltage below 27.0 VDC, descend to LM lifeboat configuration immediately. Power down CSM non-essential loads to conserve remaining cell capacity for re-entry.

title: O2 cryo tank pressure rise during stir
body: 1. Acknowledge master alarm and confirm with crew. 2. Close affected O2 tank isolation valve (SM REAC). 3. De-energize tank heaters and stir fans. 4. Verify O2 tank 1 pressure / quantity sensor validity. 5. Monitor fuel cells for reactant supply degradation. 6. Prepare LM lifeboat checklist as contingency.

title: Apollo 13 cryo tank rupture (1970-04-13, GET 55:54:53)
body: Routine cryo-stir command at GET 55:53:18 ignited Teflon insulation in O2 tank 2 due to prior heater short. Tank 2 pressure ramped 887 -> 1008 psia over 95 seconds, then ruptured. Tank 1 secondary leak began at GET 55:57:00. Fuel cells 1 and 3 lost reactant pressure at GET 55:58:06. Crew transferred to LM Aquarius as lifeboat. Lessons: heater protection circuits insufficient; manual stir during transit risky if tank state uncertain.
citation: Cortright Commission Report NASA SP-1969 (1970); Mission Report MSC-02680 §5
